core_obligations: Record that base change preserves universal injectivity and that the property is Zariski local on the base (proof lines 5890-5892).
Reduce to a flat surjective morphism of affines and fix a field K with two morphisms a, b : Spec(K) -> X agreeing after composition with f (proof lines 5893-5898).
Produce a field extension K'/K and a morphism Spec(K') -> S' filling the diagram, using surjectivity of S' -> S (proof lines 5898-5902).
Use the cartesian square to obtain the dotted arrows a' and b', apply universal injectivity of X' -> S' to get a' = b', and conclude a = b (proof lines 5914-5919).
Apply the general descending-properties lemma, and record the alternative proof through the diagonal (proof lines 5920-5930).
proof_roadmap: The reduction and the pointwise criterion (proof lines 5893-5898).
The field-extension diagram and the chase (proof lines 5898-5919).
Conclusion, plus the alternative diagonal proof (proof lines 5920-5930).
difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts that the property 'f is universally injective' is fpqc local on the base (statement lines 5883-5887). The proof is displayed in full for the only case that needs work: after the base-change and Zariski-locality remarks, a flat surjective morphism of affines S' -> S with universally injective base change is considered, and the defining condition is verified pointwise -- given a field K and two morphisms a, b : Spec(K) -> X with the same image in S, surjectivity of S' -> S produces a field extension K'/K and a morphism Spec(K') -> S' filling in the diagram, the cartesian square yields the two dotted arrows a', b', universal injectivity of X' -> S' forces a' = b', and the discussion of points forces a = b; the general descending-properties lemma then concludes. The author also records an alternative proof through the diagonal characterisation and locality of surjectivity, ending with a hint (proof lines 5889-5930). The level is H3: a complete diagram chase with the field-extension step made explicit.
